title: Spain: Injuries reported after high speed trains collide
summary: Several people have reportedly been injured following a train crash in southern Spain. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

image.caption: Several people have reportedly been injured following a train crash in southern Spain.Image: Bruna Casas/REUTERS

blocks.text: Spanish train services between Madrid and Seville were suspended on Wednesday morning after an accident involving two trains which resulted in an unspecified number of injuries.

"There has been a collision between two trains [and] there are injured people," said Manuel Galans, mayor of the town of Urda in the province of Toledo where the incident took place just after 9 a.m. local time.
"Traffic ​on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line ​has been suspended following a rear-end collision ​between two trains," confirmed rail operator Adif in a post on social media.
Spanish newspaper El Pais cited witnesses describing numerous injuries and ​arrival of emergency medical teams at the scene.
Two of the train carriages involved reportedly ​left the tracks between ​Urda and Yebenes and tumbled down an embankment, the report added.
It's not the first train crash in Spain this year. In January, 45 people died when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train.
